projects.name: Foster Creek
projects.dek: Foster Creek is a steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) oil sands project in northeast Alberta producing diluted bitumen. It is one of Cenovus's two core in-situ assets alongside Christina Lake.
projects.production_vintage: AER ST3/ST53 actuals through Jul 2026, pulled 2026-09-22

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Cenovus Energy Inc. owns 100% and operates Foster Creek, effective May 17, 2017, when ConocoPhillips completed the sale of its 50% non-operated interest in the Foster Creek Christina Lake (FCCL) partnership to Cenovus. (Source: ConocoPhillips, ConocoPhillips Completes Sale of Foster Creek Christina Lake Partnership Interest and Western Canada Deep Basin Gas Assets to Cenovus, 2017-05-17)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Nameplate capacity is 210,000 bbl/d of bitumen, after a debottlenecking/optimization program. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Cenovus grows capacity at Foster Creek and upsizes expansion at Christina Lake North, 2026-02-20)
• Demonstrated output has exceeded the stated nameplate: all-time maximum 245,300 bbl/d in July 2026 (AER ST53, scheme "Foster Creek"). Modeled nameplate confirmed at 210,000 bbl/d, 2026-09-23: credible and conservative against demonstrated history. Per the standing rule, where actuals beat announced nameplate, history wins.

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• A sanctioned solvent-aided project is expected to add 5,000 to 10,000 bbl/d of production by 2028. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Second quarter 2026 results, 2026-07-29)
• A sulphur recovery project at Foster Creek was completed, with disclosed expected cost savings of $0.50 to $0.75 per barrel. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Second quarter 2026 results, 2026-07-29)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • A turnaround was conducted at Foster Creek in Q2 2026. Note: secondary-sourced; primary disclosure of planned turnaround frequency and duration was not found in reviewed sources. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Cenovus grows capacity at Foster Creek and upsizes expansion at Christina Lake North, 2026-02-20)

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body: • Per-barrel operating cost for Foster Creek specifically was not disclosed. Cenovus disclosed that the completed sulphur project is expected to reduce costs by $0.50 to $0.75/bbl. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Second quarter 2026 results, 2026-07-29)

sections.heading: Technology and process
sections.body: • SAGD with solvent co-injection optimization. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Second quarter 2026 results, 2026-07-29)

sections.heading: Regulatory status
sections.body: • Operating. The project is part of the Foster Creek Christina Lake partnership scheme and is an established operating facility. Planned turnaround frequency and duration: not disclosed.

sections.heading: Upcoming maintenance
sections.body: • 2026-10-01 to 2026-12-31: none found — impact unquantified (guidance sourced)

projects.name: Christina Lake
projects.dek: Christina Lake is a steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) project in northeast Alberta producing diluted bitumen. It is Cenovus's largest in-situ asset. It is a separate project from Christina Lake North (the former MEG Energy asset), which is tracked separately under meg_christina_lake; the two share the same ST53 scheme name but are different facilities with different ownership histories.

(Source: ConocoPhillips, ConocoPhillips Completes Sale of Foster Creek Christina Lake Partnership Interest and Western Canada Deep Basin Gas Assets to Cenovus, 2017-05-17)

sections.body: • Nameplate capacity of 260,000 bbl/d of bitumen, based on AER and facility-operator data. Note: secondary-sourced. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Christina Lake project profile, 2026-08-11)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• The Narrows Lake lease was developed as a tie-back into the Christina Lake central processing facility via a 17-km connection (about $300 million). First oil was achieved in July 2025; AER ST53 reports Narrows Lake as its own scheme, ramping from 1.2 kb/d in Jul 2025 to 80.2 kb/d in Jul 2026, above the original 20,000 to 30,000 bbl/d company guidance. Narrows Lake is tracked as its own model leaf (narrows_lake) with its forecast from observed history; no generic growth is added on top. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Q3 2024 results news release, 2024-10-31, https://www.cenovus.com/News-and-Stories/News-releases/2024/2972380; Source: Alberta Major Projects, Narrows Lake Tie-Back to Christina Lake, https://majorprojects.alberta.ca/details/Narrows-Lake-Tie-Back-to-Christina-Lake/11241; AER ST53, verified 2026-09-23)
• At the separate Christina Lake North facility, the first of two new steam generators was expected online by year-end 2026, with redevelopment production expected to rise in the second half of 2026. See meg_christina_lake for the North facility. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Second quarter 2026 results, 2026-07-29)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • Maintenance work impacted production at Christina Lake in Q2 2023 (average 234,900 bbl/d in the quarter, down 2,300 bbl/d quarter over quarter); no additional maintenance was planned at the facility for the remainder of 2023. Planned turnaround frequency and duration not disclosed in reviewed sources. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Cenovus outlines optimization plans for its SAGD assets, 2023-07-27)

sections.body: • Per-barrel operating cost for Christina Lake specifically: not disclosed.

sections.heading: Technology and process

sections.heading: Regulatory status

The Narrows Lake tie-back was integrated into the existing Christina Lake facility (Narrows Lake was originally planned as a stand-alone 130,000 bbl/d SAGD facility but was never sanctioned). (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Cenovus outlines optimization plans for its SAGD assets, 2023-07-27)

projects.name: Sunrise
projects.dek: Sunrise is a steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) oil sands project in northeast Alberta producing diluted bitumen. Cenovus acquired full ownership from bp in 2022 and has been applying its oil sands operating model to raise output beyond original nameplate.
projects.production_vintage: AER ST3/ST53 actuals through Jul 2026, pulled 2026-09-22

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Cenovus Energy Inc. owns 100% and operates Sunrise. Cenovus announced on June 13, 2022 that it had reached an agreement to purchase the remaining 50% of the Sunrise oil sands project from bp for $600 million in cash plus a variable payment and Cenovus's 35% position in the undeveloped Bay du Nord project offshore Newfoundland and Labrador. The transaction had an effective date of May 1, 2022 and was anticipated to close in Q3 2022. Cenovus had operated Sunrise since the beginning of 2021 following the Husky Energy transaction. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Cenovus acquiring outstanding 50% interest in Sunrise oil sands asset, 2022-06-13)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body: • Nameplate capacity of 60,000 bbl/d of bitumen at the time of the 2022 acquisition, with Cenovus expecting to achieve it through a multi-year development program. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Cenovus acquiring outstanding 50% interest in Sunrise oil sands asset, 2022-06-13)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• Cenovus targets Sunrise output of approximately 70,000 bbl/d by 2028. CONFIRMED by primary corporate disclosure: "production continues to ramp up towards 70,000 bbls/d by 2028"; the first of four new well pads on the east development area began producing in April 2026, with a second pad expected online later in 2026. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Cenovus announces first-quarter 2026 results news release, 2026-05-06)
• APPLIED to the model 2026-09-23 (the editor): the cve_sunrise project leaf is held at 70.0 kb/d flat across all forecast months (Oct 2026-Dec 2027), replacing the declining seasonal baseline. Current output ~68 kb/d (ST53, 2026-07).
• Cenovus stated in 2022 that applying its operating techniques should increase Sunrise production while driving down sustaining capital, operating costs, and emissions intensity. (Source: Cenovus Energy, Cenovus acquiring outstanding 50% interest in Sunrise oil sands asset, 2022-06-13)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • The turnaround interval at Sunrise was increased from four years to five years, and the next major turnaround is not expected until 2030. Note: secondary-sourced from an earnings-call recap; primary-source confirmation recommended. (Source: The Cerbat Gem, Cenovus Energy Q4 earnings call highlights, 2026-02-19)

projects.name: Jackfish
projects.dek: Jackfish is a steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) in-situ oil sands project in the Athabasca region producing bitumen. Canadian Natural acquired it from Devon Energy in 2019.
projects.production_vintage: AER ST3/ST53 actuals through Jul 2026, pulled 2026-09-22

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Canadian Natural Resources Limited owns 100% and operates Jackfish. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2026 results front-end, 2026-05-07)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Announced nameplate capacity of 120,000 bbl/d of bitumen. The facility runs ABOVE announced nameplate: all-time demonstrated maximum 131,300 bbl/d in July 2026 (AER ST53, scheme "Jackfish", Canadian Natural Resources Limited); the facility has at times operated above nameplate (e.g., a record 129,000 bbl/d at the end of 2020). Modeled nameplate is 131,000 bbl/d (demonstrated output), raised 2026-09-23 per the standing rule: where actuals beat announced nameplate, history wins and the page says so explicitly. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2026 results front-end, 2026-05-07; Oil Sands Magazine, CNRL makes plans to add 'low risk volumes' to its thermal portfolio, 2021-11-14; Source: AER ST53 monthly, verified 2026-09-23)
• Note: the ST53 scheme "Jackfish 1" under Devon NEC Corporation (max 32,100 bbl/d, 2010-12) is a separate legacy scheme and is NOT part of the Jackfish project total. The Devon Canada Corporation "Jackfish" row (max 128,200 bbl/d, 2018-12) is the pre-acquisition record of the same physical asset now operated by CNRL.

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• At Pike (adjacent lease, now 100% CNRL after the Q1 2022 acquisition of the remaining 50% working interest), two SAGD pads were being drilled in H1 2025 and will be tied into the existing Jackfish facilities; both were targeted to come on production in 2026 to keep the Jackfish plants at full capacity. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2025 interim report, 2025-05-08)
• Canadian Natural reports total thermal in-situ facility processing capacity of approximately 340,000 bbl/d across its portfolio (not allocable to individual projects). (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2025 interim report, 2025-05-08)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body:
• A turnaround at Jackfish was completed in April 2026, with a Q2 average impact of about 9,300 bbl/d. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2026 results front-end, 2026-05-07)
• Planned turnaround frequency: not disclosed.

projects.name: Leismer
projects.dek: Leismer is a steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD) oil sands project in the Athabasca region, operated by Athabasca Oil Corporation. It is undergoing an expansion to 40,000 bbl/d by end of 2027.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Athabasca Oil Corporation owns 100% and operates Leismer. (Source: Athabasca Oil Corporation, Athabasca Oil Announces its 2026 Budget Focused on Production and Cash Flow Per Share Growth, via GlobeNewswire, 2025-12-11)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body: • Expansion targets 40,000 bbl/d of production by end of 2027, on a ~$300 million expansion project at about $25,000/bbl/d capital efficiency. (Source: Athabasca Oil Corporation, Athabasca Oil Announces its 2026 Budget Focused on Production and Cash Flow Per Share Growth, via GlobeNewswire, 2025-12-11)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• The $300 million expansion project includes bringing on twelve new wells at Pads L10 and L11, adding two steam generators, heat exchangers, and increased fluid handling capacity. The expansion was expected to be substantially complete at end of 2026, with production growth to 40,000 bbl/d by end of 2027; capital and schedule were on track with original expectations. (Source: Athabasca Oil Corporation, Athabasca Oil Announces its 2026 Budget Focused on Production and Cash Flow Per Share Growth, via GlobeNewswire, 2025-12-11)
• A later Leismer Phase 1 had not yet been formally sanctioned and awaited fiscal-framework confirmation as of Q2 2026; this is distinct from the already-underway 40,000 bbl/d expansion. (Source: Athabasca Oil Corporation, Q2 2026 press release, 2026-07-29)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • A three-week facility turnaround was completed in May 2026 (four-year interval); all tie-ins for the expansion project were also completed during it. The new well pairs began steaming after the turnaround. (Source: Athabasca Oil Corporation, Athabasca Oil Announces its 2026 Budget Focused on Production and Cash Flow Per Share Growth, via GlobeNewswire, 2025-12-11)

sections.heading: Operating costs

projects.dek: Primrose is a cyclic steam stimulation (CSS) in-situ project in the Grand Rapids formation, 65 km north of Bonnyville inside the Cold Lake Air Weapons Range; the Wolf Lake development is also included in the facility. The project has operated below capacity since a bitumen flow-to-surface incident in spring 2013, which was deemed to be caused by excessive steaming; Canadian Natural has since modified steaming strategies, enhanced pressure monitoring, and moved to low-pressure steamflood remediation.

(Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q4 2024 and year-end results, via markets.financialcontent.com, 2025-03-06)
• One CSS pad was expected in Q3 2026 and two more in 2027. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q4 2025 results front-end, document date not verified in this pass)

sections.heading: Maintenance

projects.name: Kearl
projects.dek: Kearl is an open-pit oil sands mining project about 75 km northeast of Fort McMurray. It uses paraffinic froth treatment (PFT) to produce diluted bitumen (Kearl Lake Dilbit) with no on-site upgrader; diluent is supplied from Edmonton via pipeline and diluted bitumen is shipped to the Edmonton area by pipeline.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Imperial Oil Resources Limited operates Kearl with a 70.96% working interest; ExxonMobil Canada holds 29.04%. (Source: Imperial Oil, Imperial provides 2026 corporate guidance outlook, via Business Wire, 2025-12-15)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• 345,000 bbl/d of bitumen recorded as the capacity basis (regulatory approval; ExxonMobil/Imperial 2013 startup announcement: ultimate production capacity about 345,000 bbl/d by about 2020). Demonstrated ST39 single-month peak of 347,800 bbl/d in July 2025 is 0.8% above basis, essentially at basis (metering noise); the capacity basis is unchanged at 345,000 bbl/d. (Source: Ledcor, Kearl Oil Sands project page, 2026-09-23; ExxonMobil, ExxonMobil Announces Production Startup at Kearl Oil Sands Project, 2013-04-27; AER ST39, verified 2026-09-23)
• The initial development (110,000 bbl/d) started production in April 2013; the expansion (110,000 bbl/d) was fully funded and targeted late 2015, with debottlenecking planned to reach the approved 345,000 bbl/d by about 2020. (Source: ExxonMobil, ExxonMobil Announces Production Startup at Kearl Oil Sands Project, 2013-04-27)
• 2026 gross production guidance is 285,000 to 295,000 bbl/d. (Source: Imperial Oil, Imperial provides 2026 corporate guidance outlook, via Business Wire, 2025-12-15)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body: • Imperial disclosed work intended to extend Kearl toward 300,000 bbl/d and to extend the turnaround interval from two years to four years. (Source: Imperial Oil, Imperial provides 2026 corporate guidance outlook, via Business Wire, 2025-12-15)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • A planned turnaround at Kearl in Q2 2026 was disclosed in the 2026 guidance. The turnaround interval is being extended from two years to four years. Specific duration not disclosed. (Source: Imperial Oil, Imperial provides 2026 corporate guidance outlook, via Business Wire, 2025-12-15)

sections.heading: Operating costs

sections.heading: Technology and process
sections.body: • Open-pit mining with paraffinic froth treatment (PFT); no on-site upgrader. Using the proprietary paraffinic froth treatment process, the need for an on-site upgrader was eliminated, significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions versus a conventional mining-plus-upgrading configuration. (Source: Canadian Mining Journal, OIL SANDS: Kearl expansion on line ahead of schedule, 2015)

projects.name: Fort Hills
projects.dek: Fort Hills is an open-pit oil sands mining project using paraffinic froth treatment (PFT) to produce Fort Hills Dilbit (FRB), which is sold directly and also fed to Suncor's Base Plant upgrader.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Suncor Energy Inc. owns 100% and operates Fort Hills. Suncor acquired TotalEnergies EP Canada Ltd.'s 31.23% working interest for $1.468 billion, announced October 4, 2023, effective April 1, 2023. The acquired interest represented about 61,000 bbl/d of net capacity. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor completes acquisition of TotalEnergies EP Canada Ltd., 2023-10-04)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Announced nameplate of 194,000 bbl/d of bitumen (Suncor-confirmed, 2018). Demonstrated output runs above it: AER ST39 peak of 208,100 bbl/d in December 2018, with the 194,000 bbl/d level beaten in 9 separate months. Per the standing nameplate rule the modeled nameplate is 208,000 bbl/d; Fort Hills runs above its announced nameplate. (Source: Suncor Energy, 2018; AER ST39, verified 2026-09-23)
• 2025 full-year production was 175,000 bbl/d gross. (Source: Suncor Energy, Q4 2025 investor presentation)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body: • No sanctioned expansion disclosed in reviewed sources. Suncor deployed the Autonomous Haulage System (AHS) at Fort Hills to optimize operations. (Source: Suncor Energy Q4 2020 results news release, 2021-02-09, https://energynow.ca/2021/02/suncor-energy-reports-fourth-quarter-2020-results/)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • Suncor's 2026 corporate guidance disclosed maintenance at Fort Hills with a quarterly production and cost effect. Specific duration not disclosed. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body: • 2026 cost guidance of $33 to $36/bbl for Fort Hills (oil sands segment basis). (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)

sections.heading: Technology and process
sections.body: • Open-pit mining with paraffinic froth treatment (PFT), producing dilbit directly. Fort Hills barrels are flexible: about one-third of output has been upgraded at Suncor's Base Plant upgrader while the balance is sold as dilbit. In Q1 2026, 66,900 bbl/d of Fort Hills bitumen was transferred to Suncor Base during the Syncrude coker outage. (Source: Petroleum Australia, TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips, Suncor oil assets project page, 2026-09-23; Suncor Energy Q1 2026 Form 6-K, via StockTitan, 2026-05)

sections.heading: Regulatory status
sections.body: • Operating.

projects.name: Horizon
projects.dek: Horizon is an integrated oil sands mining and upgrading project north of Fort McMurray. Mined bitumen is upgraded on site to synthetic crude oil (SCO). Canadian Natural reports three distinct capacity bases for Horizon: mined-bitumen capacity, operating SCO capacity, and regulatory SCO nameplate. These are different figures and must not be mixed.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Canadian Natural Resources Limited owns 100% of the Horizon mine and upgrader and is the operator. Canadian Natural acquired the remaining working interests in the Athabasca Oil Sands Project assets from Shell and Marathon, and since March 1, 2025 it holds 100% of the Albian mines (Jackpine and Muskeg River). It also holds an 80% non-operated interest in the Scotford Upgrader (Shell 20%, operator), a separate upgrading asset. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, acquisition announcement, via BOE Report, 2017-03-09)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Mined-bitumen capacity of 314,000 bbl/d. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, CNRL Horizon Mine project profile, 2026-09-23)
• SCO operating capacity of 264,000 bbl/d, following the 2024 Reliability Enhancement Project. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2025 interim report, 2025-05-08)
• Regulatory SCO nameplate of 271,000 bbl/d. Note: secondary-sourced. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, 2026 production forecast: oil sands mining and upgrading, 2026-01-15)
• Demonstrated peaks exceed all three stated bases: 309,800 bbl/d SCO in November 2025 and 333,300 bbl/d mined bitumen in May 2026 (AER ST39, "CNRL HORIZON OIL SANDS PROJECT", Production). The model's capacity reference for headroom/utilization math uses these demonstrated peaks; the three stated bases are recorded as stated. Per the standing rule, where actuals beat announced capacity, history wins. Mine-bitumen capacity and upgrader SCO capacity are kept as separate lines, never blended.

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body:
• The NRUTT (Naphtha Recovery Unit Tailings Treatment) project targets an incremental 6,300 bbl/d of SCO in Q3 2027. APPLIED 2026-09-23 (the editor): +6.3 kb/d step change on the Horizon SCO leaf for Jul-Sep 2027 (the Q3/27 months in the Oct 2026-Dec 2027 forecast window); step change, not a ramp. The previously flagged implied ~277,300 bbl/d post-NRUTT nameplate is moot: demonstrated ST39 peak is 309.8 kb/d SCO (2025-11) and history wins per the standing rule, so only the +6.3 increment is modeled. (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, "Canadian Natural Resources Limited Announces 2026 Budget", 2025-12-16: "At Horizon, the Company is progressing its Naphtha Recovery Unit Tailings Treatment ("NRUTT") project that targets incremental production in Q3/27 of approximately 6,300 bbl/d of SCO following mechanical completion."; verbatim company release text via newswire mirrors including https://www.advfn.com/stock-market/TSX/CNQ/stock-news/97449467/canadian-natural-resources-limited-announces-2026)
• In November 2025 Canadian Natural unveiled over $15 billion in oil sands expansion plans; project-level allocation to Horizon was not detailed in the reviewed summary. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, 2025-11-11, referenced in the Peace River project profile, accessed 2026-09-23, https://www.oilsandsmagazine.com/projects/cnrl-peace-river)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • A 35-day turnaround begins September 2026, with an annual-average impact of 29,000 bbl/d. The turnaround runs on a two-year cycle, with the next one targeted for 2028. (Source: BOE Report, Canadian Natural Resources Limited announces 2026 budget, 2025-12-16)

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body: • Oil Sands Mining and Upgrading operating cost of C$21.88/bbl of SCO in Q1 2025 (segment basis covering Horizon, not project-allocated). (Source: Canadian Natural Resources Limited, Q1 2025 interim report, 2025-05-08)

sections.heading: Technology and process
sections.body: • Open-pit mining with naphtha froth treatment (NFT); mined bitumen is upgrader-locked and is upgraded on site to SCO. Note: NFT classification is secondary-sourced research. (Source: project technology research compilation, 2026-09-23)

sections.heading: Regulatory status
sections.body: • Operating. The NRUTT (Naphtha Recovery Unit Tailings Treatment) project is sanctioned with a Q3 2027 in-service target. (Source: BOE Report, Canadian Natural Resources Limited announces 2026 budget, 2025-12-16)

sections.heading: Upcoming maintenance
sections.body: • 2028-01-01 to 2028-12-31: forward schedule — impact unquantified (guidance sourced)

projects.name: Base Plant
projects.dek: Base Plant (Oil Sands Base) is Suncor's integrated mining and upgrading complex north of Fort McMurray. Mined bitumen is upgraded on site to synthetic crude oil (SCO). It is part of Suncor's Oil Sands Operations segment and connects to the Syncrude and Fort Hills assets via bi-directional interconnecting pipelines brought into service in Q4 2020.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • Suncor Energy Inc. owns 100% and operates Base Plant. (Source: Suncor Energy, Q4 2025 investor presentation)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Upgrader capacity of 350,000 bbl/d of SCO. (Source: Suncor Energy, Q4 2025 investor presentation)
• Base Mine production was 262,000 bbl/d of bitumen in 2025. (Source: Suncor Energy, Q4 2025 investor presentation)
• Convention (confirmed 2026-09-23): mine-bitumen capacity and upgrader SCO capacity are kept as separate lines in the model and on the project page, never blended into a single capacity figure.

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body: • No sanctioned capacity expansion disclosed in reviewed sources. Suncor disclosed a cogeneration project at Oil Sands Base to replace existing coke-fired boilers (part of its environmental and free-funds-flow program). (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor reports fourth quarter 2020 results, 2021-02-09)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body:
• Suncor's 2026 corporate guidance disclosed maintenance at Base Plant with a quarterly production and cost effect. Specific duration not disclosed. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)
• The Upgrader 2 major five-year turnaround was completed in 2023; the Base Plant upgrader achieved 90% full-year utilization in 2023 including that turnaround. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy achieves 2023 upstream production corporate guidance, 2024-01-03)

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body: • Per-barrel operating cost for Base Plant specifically: not disclosed. Suncor's 2026 Oil Sands Operations cost guidance (Base Plant, Firebag, MacKay River) is $26 to $29/bbl. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)

projects.name: Syncrude
projects.dek: Syncrude is an integrated oil sands mining and upgrading joint venture in the Athabasca region (Mildred Lake and Aurora mines, upgrader). Suncor assumed operatorship in October 2021. Mined bitumen is upgraded on site to synthetic crude oil (SCO).

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • The joint venture partners are Suncor Energy Inc. (58.74%), Imperial Oil Resources Limited (25.0%), Sinopec Oil Sands Partnership (9.03%), and CNOOC Oil Sands Canada (7.23%). Suncor's interest grew from 53.74% to 58.74% when it closed the purchase of Mocal Energy's 5% interest on February 26, 2018, effective January 1, 2018. Suncor is the operator (since October 2021). (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy closes purchase of additional interest in Syncrude, via GlobeNewswire/BOE Report, 2018-02-26; International Mining, Suncor officially takes over operatorship of Syncrude Joint Venture, 2021-10-08)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• Gross SCO capacity of about 350,000 bbl/d. (Source: JX Nippon Oil and Gas Exploration, Summary of Syncrude Oil Sand Project, 2026-09-23; Oil and Gas Journal, Suncor buys Mocal Energy's Syncrude stake, 2018-02-12)
• Suncor reports its share of upgrader capacity as 206,000 bbl/d, net to its 58.74% working interest (206,000 / 0.5874 implies about 350,700 bbl/d gross; the company does not state the gross figure, so record both bases without treating them as a conflict). (Source: Suncor Energy, Q4 2025 investor presentation)
• Syncrude gross production averaged 323,000 bbl/d in 2023 (190,000 bbl/d net to Suncor). (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy achieves 2023 upstream production corporate guidance, 2024-01-03)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body: • No sanctioned expansion disclosed in reviewed sources.

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body:
• Suncor's 2026 corporate guidance disclosed maintenance at Syncrude with a quarterly production and cost effect. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)
• A planned turnaround at Syncrude in Q2 2026 was disclosed in Imperial Oil's 2026 guidance; Imperial's 2026 Syncrude production guidance is 78,000 to 82,000 bbl/d (Imperial share). (Source: Imperial Oil, Imperial provides 2026 corporate guidance outlook, via Business Wire, 2025-12-15)
• The Q1 2026 Syncrude coker outage demonstrated the interconnect playbook: 16,400 bbl/d of Syncrude bitumen and 66,900 bbl/d of Fort Hills bitumen were transferred to Suncor Base, with the Base upgrader running at 108% utilization. (Source: Suncor Energy Q1 2026 Form 6-K, via StockTitan, 2026-05)
• The Suncor Base-Syncrude interconnect pipelines are BI-DIRECTIONAL per Suncor (Nov 2020 operatorship announcement). Flow is not limited to Syncrude-to-Base; Suncor mine bitumen can feed the Syncrude upgrader as well. (Source: Suncor Energy news release via Oilfield Technology, 2020-11-24, https://www.oilfieldtechnology.com/drilling-and-production/24112020/suncor-to-assume-syncrude-operatorship-by-end-of-2021/)

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body:
• 2026 cost guidance of $34 to $37/bbl, net to Suncor's 58.74% share. (Source: Suncor Energy, Suncor Energy announces 2026 corporate guidance, 2025-12-11)
• Imperial Oil reported Q2 2026 unit cash cost of C$57.81/bbl for its Syncrude share. (Source: Investing News, Imperial announces second quarter 2026 financial and operating results, 2026-07-31)

projects.name: Long Lake Upgrader
projects.dek: Long Lake is an integrated SAGD and upgrader complex about 40 km southeast of Fort McMurray. The upgrader was idled in 2016 after a fatal explosion in January 2016; since then, the SAGD operation has sold diluted bitumen directly to market and the project functions as a SAGD-only producer. This file covers the complex; the ST53 scheme "Long Lake" tracks the SAGD bitumen line.

sections.heading: Operator and ownership
sections.body: • CNOOC Petroleum North America ULC (CPNA, formerly Nexen Energy ULC) is the 100% owner and operator; CPNA is a wholly owned subsidiary of China National Offshore Oil Company Limited (CNOOC). (Source: Alberta Energy Regulator, CNOOC Long Lake and Kinosis annual performance presentation, 2021-06-30)

sections.heading: Capacity
sections.body:
• SAGD design bitumen capacity of 11,130 m3/d, i.e., 70,000 bbl/d; steam capacity of 37,000 m3/d (233,000 bbl/d). (Source: Alberta Energy Regulator, CNOOC Long Lake and Kinosis annual performance presentation, 2021-06-30)
• The SAGD facility is separately reported with capacity of 90,000 bbl/d. Note: secondary-sourced. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Long Lake project profile, 2026-09-23)
• Upgrader nameplate of 58,000 bbl/d of SCO, idled in 2016. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Long Lake Upgrader project profile, 2026-09-23)

sections.heading: Growth and expansions
sections.body: • An application to restart the idled upgrader was filed with the AER in November 2021, marked "reassigned" on January 17, 2022, with a partial resumption targeted by March 2022. The current status of the restart was not disclosed in reviewed sources. (Source: CPECN/Bloomberg, Long Lake Upgrader To Be Restarted Six Years After Fatal Explosion, 2022-01)

sections.heading: Maintenance
sections.body: • Planned turnaround frequency and duration: not disclosed.

sections.heading: Operating costs
sections.body: • Per-barrel operating cost: not disclosed.

sections.heading: Technology and process
sections.body:
• SAGD (Wabiskaw-McMurray deposit); current product is diluted bitumen. (Source: Alberta Energy Regulator, CNOOC Long Lake and Kinosis annual performance presentation, 2021-06-30)
• The idled upgrader used OPTI's proprietary OrCrude technology with solvent deasphalting, at 83% bitumen yield. (Source: Oil Sands Magazine, Long Lake Upgrader project profile, 2026-09-23)

sections.heading: Regulatory status
sections.body: • Operating as a SAGD-only scheme under scheme approval 9485 (as amended). The upgrader is idled; a restart application was filed in November 2021 and its status is not disclosed in reviewed sources. (Source: Alberta Energy Regulator, CNOOC Long Lake and Kinosis annual performance presentation, 2021-06-30; CPECN/Bloomberg, Long Lake Upgrader To Be Restarted Six Years After Fatal Explosion, 2022-01)
